senses.gloss: To recover and rise again after a fall in price, strength, or score.
senses.ru: оживать, восстанавливаться (о рынке, ценах); отыгрываться, отыграться
examples: Stocks usually *rally* when interest rates fall.
The team *rallied* from seventeen points down to win.
The market has *rallied* for three straight weeks.

senses.gloss: To move freely over a wide area, or to live naturally across a region.
examples: Wild horses still *range* across parts of Nevada.
Grizzlies once *ranged* as far south as Mexico.
The cattle were *ranging* freely over open land.

senses.gloss: To hit something quickly and sharply, making a knocking sound.
examples: *Rap* on the glass if the door is locked.
Someone *rapped* twice on the window.
The teacher was *rapping* her pen against the desk.

senses.gloss: To make someone lose their confidence or calm.
senses.ru: нервировать, выбивать из колеи; смущать, смутить
examples: Hecklers don't *rattle* her at all.
The sharp question clearly *rattled* the witness.
He has never been *rattled* by a big crowd.

senses.gloss: To make a hope, a plan, or an ability become real.
examples: It took twenty years to *realize* her dream of opening a bakery.
He never *realized* his full potential as a player.
The project has finally been *realized*, ten years after it was proposed.

senses.gloss: To get a profit or an amount of money from a sale or an investment.
examples: They hope to *realize* a profit of two million dollars.
She *realized* three hundred thousand dollars on the sale of the house.
The fund has *realized* solid gains this year.

senses.gloss: To cut and gather a crop from a field.
examples: In August the farmers *reap* the wheat.
They *reaped* the last field just before the storm.
The barley had already been *reaped* by the time we arrived.

senses.gloss: To put a substance on a surface again.
examples: *Reapply* sunscreen every two hours.
She *reapplied* her lipstick in the mirror.
The wax has to be *reapplied* once the first coat dries.

senses.gloss: To rise up on the back legs, or to rise high above everything around.
examples: Horses *rear* when something frightens them.
The stallion *reared* when the gun went off.
The snake was *rearing* up to strike.

senses.gloss: To start a movie or TV series over with a new cast and a new version of the story.
examples: The studio plans to *reboot* the franchise next year.
They *rebooted* the series with a much younger cast.
The show is being *rebooted* for a streaming service.

senses.gloss: To bounce back after hitting a surface.
examples: Sound *rebounds* off the bare walls.
The ball *rebounded* off the rim and into his hands.
The puck was *rebounding* around the boards.

senses.gloss: To order that a faulty product be returned by the people who bought it.
examples: If the part fails, the maker must *recall* it.
The company *recalled* forty thousand cars last spring.
Two brands of baby formula have been *recalled*.

senses.gloss: To remove an elected official from office through a special vote.
examples: Voters can *recall* a governor before the term ends.
They *recalled* two members of the school board.
The mayor was *recalled* in a special election.

senses.gloss: To react to something or someone in a particular way.
examples: How will voters *receive* the plan?
The audience *received* the speech warmly.
Her first novel was well *received* by critics.

senses.gloss: To rest until you get your energy back.
examples: I need a few days off to *recharge*.
She *recharged* over the long weekend.
He came back from the trip completely *recharged*.

senses.gloss: To make land or material usable again, by draining it or by saving it from waste.
senses.ru: осваивать, отвоёвывать (землю); восстанавливать для повторного использования
examples: The city wants to *reclaim* the old rail yard for housing.
The Dutch *reclaimed* much of their farmland from the sea.
The floors are made of *reclaimed* barn wood.

senses.gloss: To give someone public credit or an award for what they have done.
examples: We want to *recognize* the people who made this possible.
The mayor *recognized* the firefighters at a ceremony downtown.
She has been *recognized* for thirty years of service.

senses.gloss: To build a friendship or a family tie again after a long time apart.
senses.ru: восстанавливать связь, снова сблизиться, наладить отношения
examples: He went home hoping to *reconnect* with his brother.
They *reconnected* at a class reunion after twenty years.
She has *reconnected* with several old friends online.

senses.gloss: To work out and describe how a past event happened, using the evidence that is left.
examples: Investigators are trying to *reconstruct* the last hour of the flight.
From the receipts, police *reconstructed* his movements that night.
The accident has been *reconstructed* frame by frame.

senses.gloss: To get well again after an illness, or to return to a normal condition after trouble.
senses.ru: выздоравливать, поправляться; восстанавливаться, прийти в себя
examples: It takes about a month to *recover* from this surgery.
He *recovered* quickly and was back at work in a week.
The economy has never fully *recovered* from the shutdown.

senses.gloss: To use old material or old ideas again instead of making something new.
examples: Don't just *recycle* last year's talk.
He *recycled* the same joke at every stop on the tour.
That plot has been *recycled* a dozen times.

senses.gloss: To make up for a mistake or a fault and win back people's good opinion.
senses.ru: искупать, искупить (вину); реабилитировать себя, исправить впечатление
examples: One good scene can't *redeem* a bad movie.
He *redeemed* himself with a touchdown in the last minute.
The film is *redeemed* by its final twenty minutes.

senses.gloss: To boil a liquid so that some of the water evaporates and the flavor gets stronger.
examples: *Reduce* the sauce until it coats the back of a spoon.
She *reduced* the stock by half.
The wine was *reducing* on the back burner.

senses.gloss: To bring someone or something down to a much worse state.
examples: Don't let him *reduce* you to tears.
The fire *reduced* the barn to a pile of ash.
Whole blocks had been *reduced* to rubble.

senses.gloss: To give a strong impression that something dishonest or unpleasant is involved.
senses.ru: попахивать, отдавать (чем-л. дурным); явно свидетельствовать о
examples: The whole arrangement *reeks* of a cover-up.
His apology *reeked* of insincerity.
The timing has always *reeked* of politics.

senses.gloss: To remove the unwanted parts from a raw material to make it pure.
examples: It costs more to *refine* heavy crude oil.
The mill *refined* the ore right where it was mined.
White bread is made from heavily *refined* flour.

senses.gloss: To throw back light, heat, or an image from a surface.
examples: Snow *reflects* most of the sunlight that hits it.
The mountains were *reflected* in the still lake.
The mirror was *reflecting* the light straight into my eyes.

senses.gloss: To show something clearly, or to be a sign of it.
examples: These numbers *reflect* only the first quarter.
The results *reflected* months of hard work.
The change is already *reflected* in this month's bill.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel less tired and more comfortable.
examples: A cold shower will *refresh* you.
The short nap *refreshed* him completely.
They came back *refreshed* after two weeks off.

senses.gloss: To bring something back into someone's memory.
examples: Let me *refresh* your memory.
The photograph *refreshed* my memory of that day.
She read her old notes, *refreshing* her memory before the exam.

senses.gloss: To not let someone have or do something they ask for.
examples: They can't *refuse* you a lawyer.
The guard *refused* us entry.
She was *refused* a visa twice.

senses.gloss: To look at someone or something steadily.
examples: He *regarded* her in silence for a long moment.
The old cat *regards* every visitor with suspicion.
She stood in the doorway, *regarding* us coolly.

senses.gloss: To put your name, or someone else's, on an official list.
senses.ru: регистрировать(ся), зарегистрироваться; записываться, ставить на учёт
examples: You have to *register* to vote thirty days before the election.
She *registered* for three classes in the fall.
The car is *registered* in his wife's name.

senses.gloss: Of an instrument or a scale: to show a particular level or amount.
examples: The thermometer never *registers* below zero here.
The quake *registered* 6.8 on the Richter scale.
Temperatures of 115 degrees were *registered* in Phoenix.

senses.gloss: To keep a level, a speed, or a flow steady and correct.
examples: Sweating helps *regulate* body temperature.
The old thermostat *regulated* the heat badly.
Blood sugar is *regulated* by insulin.

senses.gloss: To bring an injured part of the body back to full strength through treatment and exercise.
examples: It can take a year to *rehabilitate* a knee like that.
He *rehabilitated* his shoulder with daily exercises.
She spent the summer *rehabilitating* a torn ligament.

senses.gloss: To be the main feature of a situation for a period of time.
examples: Silence *reigns* in the reading room.
Chaos *reigned* for the rest of the afternoon.
Confusion has *reigned* since the announcement.

senses.gloss: To hold a championship or a title at the present time.
examples: She *reigned* as world champion for five years.
The *reigning* Super Bowl champions open the season at home.
No one has *reigned* that long in the sport.

senses.gloss: To make a belief, a habit, or an impression stronger.
examples: Praise *reinforces* good behavior better than punishment.
The trip *reinforced* my decision to move.
The stereotype is *reinforced* by every movie about the place.

senses.gloss: Of the body: to fail to accept a transplanted organ.
examples: Her body *rejected* the first kidney.
These drugs keep the body from *rejecting* the new heart.
The transplant was *rejected* within a week.

senses.gloss: To start drinking, using drugs, or repeating a bad habit again after stopping.
senses.ru: срываться, сорваться; возвращаться к прежней привычке
examples: Most people *relapse* at least once.
He *relapsed* after eight months sober.
She has *relapsed* twice since the program ended.

senses.gloss: To tell someone about events, in order.
examples: *Relate* the events exactly as you remember them.
He *related* the whole story over dinner.
She spent an hour *relating* what had happened that night.

senses.gloss: To make a rule or a restriction less strict.
examples: Officials may *relax* the rules next month.
The city *relaxed* its parking limits over the holiday.
Several states are *relaxing* their licensing requirements.

senses.gloss: To move someone or something to a lower, less important position.
senses.ru: отодвигать на второй план, задвигать; переводить на менее важное место
examples: Don't *relegate* the idea to a footnote.
A knee injury *relegated* him to the bench.
The story was *relegated* to page twelve.

senses.gloss: To put more ammunition into a gun.
examples: He had to *reload* after six shots.
She *reloaded* and fired again.
The soldier was *reloading* behind the wall.

senses.gloss: To continue to be in the same state or condition.
senses.ru: оставаться (каким-л.), сохраняться в том же состоянии
examples: Please *remain* seated until the plane comes to a stop.
She *remained* calm through the whole flight.
The cause of the fire has *remained* a mystery.

senses.gloss: To be left after the rest is gone or used up.
examples: Only three tickets *remain*.
Little *remained* of the house after the fire.
The stone foundation is all that has *remained* of the mill.
